einstellungen.text: At twelve twelve AM, your night bus shows a stop that doesn't exist.
Your driver, Henrik, glances in the rearview mirror. At the sign. Then at you.
His face goes white as chalk.
“Millbrook Lane hasn't existed since nineteen ninety-eight.”
He says it like he's thought those words a thousand times.
Five minutes earlier, twelve oh seven. Your best friend Ben walks you from his birthday party to the last bus.
“Text me when you're home. Or I'm calling your mom.”
The bus is empty. Just you and the hum of the lights.
Henrik has driven this route for thirty years. All he wants now is to clock out.
The windows fog up. Outside, the city melts into single lights.
Ben texts one more time: thanks for coming. Your battery is at twenty-three percent.
Then it's twelve twelve. And the display changes.
You know every stop on this route. There is no Millbrook Lane.
Outside, there's suddenly fog. No more houses. No more streetlights.
Nobody pressed the button. But up front, the red stop light is glowing.
Henrik's foot isn't on the brake. And still the bus is slowing down.
The bus stops. All on its own. And the doors open.
